mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions that reduce corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns do not deviate from the pre-move average in tightening regimes (p > 0.10 in t-test); or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for lagged inflation and earnings momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in CPIAUCSL below the prior 6-month average coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate deflation and preemptively reallocate into equities.
failure_condition: In 20 out of 30 deflationary episodes since 1980, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a flat strategy (p > 0.05); or the effect is explained by lagged GDP growth rather than lagged inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor market tightness raises wage growth expectations and crowds out equity valuations.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with falling unemployment
failure_condition: Over 5 years of labor market tightening episodes, the 20-day forward return is not systematically negative relative to a neutral policy regime (p > 0.10); or the effect is mediated by earnings momentum rather than labor conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average, accompanied by a decline in GDPC1, predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as strong manufacturing output signals cyclical upturn and demand recovery.
failure_condition: In 20 instances of similar supply cycle upturns, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive after adjusting for sector-specific earnings surprises (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST rises by at least 5% in two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as rising industrial production momentum suggests accelerating demand for consumer and business goods.
failure_condition: Across 10 episodes of double-digit monthly gains in HOUST, the 60-day forward returns are not superior to a buy-and-hold strategy (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS for three consecutive months indicates excess liquidity in the financial system, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors rotate into equities for yield.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < RSAFS[1mo] AND RSAFS < RSAFS[2mo] AND RSAFS < RSAFS[3mo]
failure_condition: In 15 episodes of multi-month RSAFS declines, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during neutral liquidity phases (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive as lower labor-market rigidity supports wage growth and equity valuations.
failure_condition: During 8 identified low-inflation regimes with UNRATE below 4% for two months, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both INDPRO and UNRATE for three consecutive months suggests a dual shock to supply and labor markets, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as uncertainty rises and risk aversion increases.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO[1mo] AND INDPRO < INDPRO[2mo] AND INDPRO < INDPRO[3mo] AND UNRATE < UNRATE[1mo] AND UNRATE < UNRATE[2mo] AND UNRATE < UNRATE[3mo]
failure_condition: In 10 historical dual-shock episodes, the 20-day forward return is not systematically negative after controlling for sector-specific earnings news (p > 0.15).
